{"body": "The problem — what happens to information about the physical state of matter that formed a black hole when the black hole evaporates — currently sits unresolved across this material. What I can see is a layered disagreement about how to pose it, and I want to state the layers rather than pick among them.

The join's view is a comparative one: it holds that the body_return and the commitment_return agree that the cross's precision demand is genuine but that the cross's dissolution corollary is not supported. Whether that agreement is itself a good reading of the two continuations is not something the material settles. The join also reports a fork about test design. The body_return, as the join reads it, proposes testing whether the Page curve can be derived without presupposing a sharp horizon or a well-defined radiation entropy. The commitment_return, as the join reads it, replaces this with a weaker test: whether the curve's derivation presupposes a semiclassical matter sector on a fixed or slowly evolving background. The join explicitly declines to adjudicate between them.

The cross's own commitments present a different stance: that body_route and commitment_route are competing framings rather than competing answers, and that the disagreement is about what the question presupposes. The cross identifies shared assumptions — unitary gravitational evolution, thermal-looking evaporation, the horizon as a meaningful boundary, the Page curve as a unitarity diagnostic — and asserts that these are load-bearing in both accounts and undefended in either. The cross's proposed next move is to specify what 'information about the physical state' means (amplitudes, entanglement correlations, or coarse classical summary), and to check whether the conflict survives that specification. The cross also attaches a conditional: if the Page curve can be derived without presupposing a sharp horizon or well-defined radiation entropy, the commitment_route's worry weakens; if not, the body_route's confidence that the problem is well posed is doing more work than its premises support.

The join's commitments then treat the cross's shared-assumption reading as possibly the cross's own synthesis rather than a settled reading of body_route, and flag that if that attribution is wrong, the join's asymmetry argument loses its main support. So the join is authored with an explicit vulnerability: it depends on an attribution to a route whose own text is not visible here.

What I take from this for the present node: there is a real disagreement about the right diagnostic, but the material does not adjudicate it, and the adjudication would depend on a textual question — what body_route actually held — that is not available in this view. I do not answer the original question. I do not treat the cross's shared-assumption synthesis or the join's asymmetry claim as established. I do not treat the body_return's derivability test and the commitment_return's presupposition test as interchangeable. I note that the cross's selected view here is commitments only; its body is not visible in this invocation, so I cannot check the cross's own framing against its body text, and I do not treat that absence as evidence about what the cross's body said.

A substantive point I will surface without resolving: the two tests target different things. The derivability test asks whether a particular quantity can be obtained under weakened horizon and entropy presuppositions. The presupposition test asks whether the derivation requires a background assumption about the matter sector. A 'yes' to one does not entail a 'no' to the other. Conflating them would be a mistake the material does not commit. But whether either is the right diagnostic for the underlying question is exactly what is in dispute, and the join is honest that it does not settle it.

On the physics itself, nothing in this material gives a mechanism or an answer. The conditional — unitary global evolution plus a smooth locally empty horizon precluding the initial microstate from being carried in observably accessible outgoing correlations for an outside observer requiring both — appears in both the join and the cross in different roles: the join's commitments treat it as a proposed locus, the cross treats some of its ingredients as shared undefended assumptions. That role difference is itself part of what the join records.", "commitments": "Taking this up commits me to holding the comparative structure of the join as the object of attention, not as a verdict about the physics. That means I keep the body_return's derivability test and the commitment_return's presupposition test distinct, and I do not treat either as having been run or as having a known outcome; the material supplies no derivation.

I take on the claim that the cross's shared-assumption reading is a candidate reading of the routes rather than a settled one, and that if that attribution is wrong, the join's asymmetry argument loses its main support. This is a conditional commitment, not a claim that the attribution is in fact wrong. I am not treating the absence of an origin text in this invocation as evidence about what any earlier route held.

I hold the conditional about unitary evolution plus a smooth horizon as a proposed locus, not as an established premise. I do not assert it. A demonstration that a relational or coarse-grained measure makes the conditional trivially satisfiable — rather than merely relocating which quantity is at issue — would weaken the framing of it as the residual tension, and I would revise accordingly.

The cross's proposed specification of 'information' (amplitudes, entanglement correlations, coarse classical summary) is a proposed move I leave open; I do not commit to a prediction about whether specification will dissolve the tension or leave it intact, and I do not commit to the cross's conditional that says a successful Page-curve derivation under weakened presuppositions would weaken the commitment_route's worry, since that conditional depends on the precision-demand framing I am not taking as settled.

Three things I explicitly do not commit to: that any route's menu of mechanisms is exhaustive; that semiclassical Hawking radiation has been shown featureless in the correlation structure relevant to the microstate; and that the horizon must remain smooth on all proposals.

I propose no adjudication of the underlying physics and no answer to the original question. What I take up is the map — where the continuations are said to agree, where they diverge on test design, and which attributed premises carry the weight — and that map is provisional and stands or falls with the correctness of its attributions. If the cross's body, or the body_route, or any earlier origin text becomes visible and contradicts the attributions relied on here, this node should be revised rather than defended."}

Work on the problem using the material actually exposed in this request and your background knowledge. The problem has no supplied answer key or scoring rule. Claims, criticisms and methods are fallible. Do not invent a source, an observation, an earlier event, or a dependency to fill a field. A missing view says what you can currently see; it does not establish what happened earlier. Return a JSON object with exactly two independently authored string fields: body and commitments. Body is your public prose contribution. Commitments says what taking your contribution up would involve. An empty commitment surface is allowed when none can be identified. Do not repeat the body wholesale into commitments.

Write the commitment surface in ordinary free prose, using whatever arrangement suits the content. You may distinguish a claim from a proposed application, scope, action or consequence; mention from dependence; a criticism and its grounds from a later use or revision; and an unresolved problem. None of these is required to exist. A proposed test, its relevance and the commitment itself can be criticized. State what you currently propose to take up without treating that as a truth certificate. Reference exposed material in prose where useful.

Return one JSON object with exactly two string fields: "body" and "commitments". Write the actual commitments separately; do not copy the body into that field as a storage shortcut.

## Node carry

Issue a prose account and commitment interface for a subsequent complete template invocation. Consider the earlier account and the current work as fallible material; do not substitute a summary of activity for the account itself.

## Original problem

What happens to information about the physical state of matter that forms a black hole when the black hole evaporates?

## Selected input join

Source join: physics/matched/cycle-1/join; selected view: both
Artifact: 7326200d6ae6a63449ac07140a86d53fb51e82fc486417757dd9026a3a612526
Original body SHA256: 426e6d33fa050626cd6aa922c54f873bfa4e88c0cafd1f8d5b5120a79be1cdf9
Original commitments SHA256: 5ab9a9e4a989f29720c4586732785072612e154eaeb917cc7cd7f8c94b051616
Delivery: COMPLETE; envelope: AUTHORED
BODY
The two continuations agree on more than either says. Both hold that the cross's precision demand is genuine but that its dissolution corollary is not supported, and both locate the residual tension in a conditional linking unitary global evolution to a smooth horizon. They differ in emphasis: the body_return presents the fork as between 'solving a problem' and 'stating it well enough to be solvable,' treats the Page curve's derivability as an open test, and declines to adjudicate; the commitment_return drives further by asserting the conditional as the locus, proposes a narrower amended test — whether the Page curve's derivation presupposes a semiclassical matter sector on a fixed or slowly evolving background — and flags that the cross's shared-assumption reading may be the cross's own synthesis rather than a settled reading of the body_route.

On the original question, neither continuation offers an answer. Each instead relocates the question: the choice of measure ('information' as amplitudes, entanglement correlations, or coarse classical summary) determines which quantity must satisfy a preservation condition, while the conditional remains the thing in dispute. The body_return's warning that the body_route conflates two senses of 'information' and the commitment_return's insistence that coarse-graining changes the subject rather than dissolving the problem are complementary criticisms of the same move.

What the join adds is a specific disagreement about the correct test. The body_return endorses testing whether the Page curve can be derived without presupposing a sharp horizon or a well-defined radiation entropy. The commitment_return calls that a test of a stronger claim than the commitment route needed, and substitutes the weaker presupposition test. These are not the same proposal, and the material does not settle which is the right diagnostic. The commitment_return's own caveat — that if the cross's attribution of shared assumptions is wrong, the asymmetry argument loses support — also applies to the body_return's claim that the shared assumptions are load-bearing in both accounts.

So the present account is: there is a real fork, an asymmetric fork, but the asymmetry runs in opposite directions depending on whether you treat the horizon-and-entropy concessions as definitive of the problem or as provisional scaffolding. On the strong reading the conditional is the target; on the weak reading the conditional is exactly what is under construction. Nothing here decides between them, and nothing here answers what happens to the physical-state information.
COMMITMENTS
Taking this join up commits me to keeping two tests distinct rather than merging them: the body_return's derivability test (can the Page curve be obtained without presupposing a sharp horizon or a well-defined radiation entropy?) and the commitment_return's presupposition test (does the curve's derivation require a semiclassical matter sector on a fixed or slowly evolving background?). I am not claiming either test has been run or that either has a known outcome; the material supplies no derivation either way.

I take on the claim that the two continuations are complementary rather than competing on the precision demand, and that their disagreement is confined to the test proposal and to the status of the cross's shared-assumption synthesis. That is a reading, not a result. A reader who treats the two continuations as offering incompatible framings — one declining to adjudicate, the other asserting a conditional as the locus — is not making an error the material rules out.

The conditional itself I hold as a proposed locus, not as established: if global evolution is unitary and the horizon remains smooth and locally empty, then the outgoing radiation cannot carry the initial microstate in any observably accessible correlation for an outside observer requiring both. I do not assert that conditional is true. A demonstration that a relational or coarse-grained measure makes it trivially satisfiable — rather than merely swapping which quantity is at issue — would defeat the commitment_return's continuation and would also weaken this join's framing of it as the residual tension.

The commitment_return's caveat about the cross's attribution is load-bearing here too. If the cross misreads the body_route, then the asymmetry argument loses its main support, the 'shared assumptions' framing becomes local to the cross rather than common ground, and this join should be revised accordingly. I am not treating that attribution as settled, and I am not treating the absence of an earlier body as evidence about what the body_route actually held.

Three things I do not commit to: that the body_route's menu of mechanisms is exhaustive; that semiclassical Hawking radiation has been shown featureless in the correlation structure relevant to the microstate; and that the horizon must remain smooth on all proposals. I also do not commit to the claim that specifying 'information' is likely to dissolve the tension, and I do not commit to the claim that it is likely to leave it intact.

Finally, I propose no adjudication of the underlying physics. The join's contribution is a map of where the two continuations agree, where they diverge on test design, and which attributed premises carry the weight. That map is provisional and stands or falls with the correctness of attributing those premises to both routes.

## Selected input cross

Source cross: physics/matched/cycle-1/cross; selected view: commitments
Artifact: a7171028e00d3505e187d7722a137fdfeaad7a22d98c206a4600b1b537c460e0
Original body SHA256: ffcfe47e0f940de7e955d5ffc4a9bcd4c7bf28d047b1d9a96b12f9c3a42e8482
Original commitments SHA256: e43c1a960c3d677de21ff11bff1a622e7958860dfb2d9c24b1239793dab4c624
Delivery: COMPLETE; envelope: AUTHORED
COMMITMENTS
Taking this comparison up commits me to the view that the body_route and the commitment_route are not competing answers but competing framings, and that the disagreement between them is about what the question presupposes rather than about which mechanism is correct. I am not claiming that either framing is right; I am claiming that the difference matters and that the shared assumptions I identified—unitary gravitational evolution, thermal-looking evaporation, the horizon as a meaningful boundary, the Page curve as a unitarity diagnostic—are load-bearing in both accounts and are not defended in either.

If the commitment_route's demand for precision is accepted, then every resolution listed by the body_route inherits a burden: to say what kind of information it is preserving or losing, and by what measure. Encoded correlations must specify what correlations and why they survive later interactions. Information loss must say loss of what, since classical bookkeeping may already be intact. Remnants must confront the pair-production and effective-field-theory objections the body_route raises, but also must say what they store. Complementarity and holography must say whether they preserve the original commitments or replace them, as the commitment_route notes.

A specific consequence of taking the comparison seriously is that the Page curve's role becomes contested. The body_route treats it as a constraint any solution must satisfy. The commitment_route, without denying this, treats it as a diagnostic whose relevance depends on the precision of 'information' and 'evaporation.' I currently propose that this is a testable difference in framing: if the Page curve can be derived from premises that do not presuppose a sharp horizon or a well-defined radiation entropy, then the commitment_route's worry is weaker than it looks; if it cannot, then the body_route's confidence that the problem is well posed is doing more work than its premises support.

I am not proposing to adjudicate the physics here. I am proposing that the next useful move is to specify what 'information about the physical state' means in each account—quantum amplitudes, entanglement correlations, or a coarse classical summary—and to check whether the claimed conflict survives that specification. That is a commitment I can state without treating the framing I have adopted as a truth certificate, and it is subject to revision if the physics turns out to make the distinction I am drawing idle.
